Accepted Stata handoff metadata: output/reproductions/packages/W3124908438/attempt_02/data/reg.dta. Metadata-only inspection found fyear present as numeric int16 with format %10.0g, labeled Compustat fiscal year; its units are fiscal-year labels, not calendar dates.
changes: Kept the original observation clock and 1984 start; extended the pooled fiscal-year cohort from 1984–2002 through the requested 2007 endpoint (2002 plus five calendar years).

Extended only the accepted construction bounds needed for the requested window: Compustat annual support through FY2008 for t+1 components, security-price input dates through 2007, CRSP security/market/delisting data through 2010 for future-return and event windows, I/B/E/S actual periods through 2008, and summary forecast periods through FPEDATS 2009 and STATPERS 2010.

Corrected the relocated Stata ado path to ../../../../../../git/output/reproductions/resources/ado and added fit-active e(sample) counts for original and added fiscal years. Stable notebook cell IDs are preserved.

Retained the original xtfmb specifications, regressors, lag(1), annual 1/99 winsorization, common complete-case screen, and all accepted construction assumptions. The fit period is rebuilt jointly from the named current local sources.

The controller completed the pooled SAS rebuild and all three Stata fits successfully. Each fit used 25,469 original-period plus 7,711 added-period rows (N=33,180), with 24 annual fits and last added FY2007; the final t+1 DATADATE reaches 31MAY2009 and the future CRSP eligibility window ends 30SEP2009.
limitations: The paper does not report the Newey–West lag order; the accepted reconstruction uses lag 1.
The paper does not say whether 1st/99th percentile winsorization is pooled or annual; the accepted reconstruction applies annual fiscal-year cutoffs.
The paper does not identify the adjusted or unadjusted I/B/E/S product; the accepted reconstruction uses unadjusted Summary History/Actuals aligned with relative CRSP CFACSHR.

The paper does not name the SIC provider; the accepted reconstruction uses valid Compustat historical SICH and a unique date-effective CRSP DSENAMES SICCD fallback only when SICH is missing or invalid.

The paper’s full all-tests-common sample is unverified because unassigned return-predictability controls and the future forecast-error outcome are not reconstructed; this job covers the three assigned fits.
The installed lagged xtfmb reports average raw R-squared and diagonal HAC coefficient variances; adjusted R-squared and valid joint HAC tests are unavailable.
The Table 8 same-or-adjacent-month forecast boundary is an operational reading of the paper’s month-window language; the paper does not uniquely specify the cutoff.

In the original 1984–2002 window, the fresh common estimation sample has 25,469 firm-year rows versus the paper-reported 38,716 overall sample, a 13,247-row discrepancy inherited from the best-effort construction. The target count is not used as a filter; the paper’s full all-tests-common sample remains unverified because unassigned analyses are not reconstructed.
